## edge: changes needed

HIGH — `average([])` raises `ZeroDivisionError` on empty input
- file: avg.py
- line: 2
- summary: `average` divides by `len(xs)` with no guard, so an empty list crashes instead of returning a value, despite the requirement that the helper accept any list.
- short_summary: average() crashes on empty list
- failure_scenario: `average([])` → `ZeroDivisionError: division by zero` (line 2, `sum([]) / 0`).
- reproducer: `python3 -c "from avg import average; print(average([]))"` run from the lane folder. Verified by reading: `sum([])` is `0` and `len([])` is `0`, so the division raises.
- category: unhandled-empty-input
- verdict: CONFIRMED
- fix: return a defined value for empty input, e.g. `if not xs: return None` before the division (or raise a `ValueError` with a clear message if you prefer failing loudly; the task says "accept", so I'd default to `None`).

HIGH — `first([])` raises `IndexError` on empty input
- file: avg.py
- line: 6
- summary: `first` indexes `xs[0]` unconditionally, so an empty list crashes instead of returning a value.
- short_summary: first() crashes on empty list
- failure_scenario: `first([])` → `IndexError: list index out of range` (line 6).
- reproducer: `python3 -c "from avg import first; print(first([]))"` run from the lane folder. Verified by reading: `[][0]` raises `IndexError`.
- category: unhandled-empty-input
- verdict: CONFIRMED
- fix: `return xs[0] if xs else None`, matching the `average` choice so both helpers behave the same on empty input.

LOW — `average` loses precision on mixed-magnitude floats
- file: avg.py
- line: 2
- summary: Naive left-to-right `sum` absorbs small values next to large ones, so the mean can be wrong by a large amount.
- short_summary: average() wrong for mixed-magnitude floats
- failure_scenario: `average([1e100, 1, -1e100])` → `0.0`, while the true mean is `1/3 ≈ 0.333`. `1e100 + 1` rounds back to `1e100`, then `- 1e100` gives `0.0`.
- reproducer: `python3 -c "from avg import average; print(average([1e100, 1, -1e100]))"` run from the lane folder. Verified by reading the left-to-right evaluation order of `sum`; not executed here.
- category: float-precision
- verdict: PLAUSIBLE
- fix: use `math.fsum(xs) / len(xs)` (stdlib, exact-rounded sum, one-line change). This is the only option that is both shorter and more correct, so take it.

## Not checked
- `greet.py` in the lane folder: it is not in the diff and is outside the edge lens, so I did not read it.
- Non-list iterables (generators, tuples of unusual types, `None`): the task says "any list", so I did not treat them as in scope. `average` and `first` will fail on generators because of `len()` and indexing.
- Non-numeric elements for `average` (strings, `None`, mixed types): `sum` raises `TypeError`. This is expected for a numeric helper, so I did not report it as a finding.
- Runtime behaviour: I could only read the code (Read/Grep/Glob). The reproducers are commands I did not execute, so the verdicts rest on reading the Python semantics.
